name: Tab Complete
desc: Player presses Tab in chat to request auto-completion. Sends the partial message or command.

fields.name: hasTargetBlock
fields.desc: Whether the cursor is over a block

fields.name: targetBlock
fields.desc: Block position the cursor is over

encoding: Whether cursor is over a block
notes: The server responds with S3APacketTabComplete containing matching commands/player names. The optional BlockPos allows for block-sensitive completions (e.g., filling /give with block IDs of looked-at block).

writeup.p: C14 requests command and player-name completions: a String (the partial input, with or without the leading slash) and an optional BlockPos for block-sensitive completions. The server replies with S3APacketTabComplete. GuiChat fires it on the tab key; the position is set when the cursor is over a block, which lets /give-style commands complete with looked-at block data.

processTabComplete calls the server command dispatcher's getTabCompletions with the message and target block, collects the returned strings and replies with S3A. There is no rate limit or throttle in the bundled 1.8.9 handler, which is what makes the packet a free information oracle: every registered command, including plugin-registered ones, is reachable through the completion namespace.

Three families across the 8 clients. (1) Plugin enumeration: Rise 5.99 Plugins sends '/' and parses S3A, with a Bypass mode that sweeps '/a'..'/z'; Sigma 4.11's PluginFinder command sends '/' once and parses the reply for ':' prefixed plugin names. (2) Crasher: Rise 5.99's FAWE mode sends a deeply nested command string. (3) Chat UX: the Rise 6.x Chat module drives its own completion via C14 with a block position.

The missing throttle is the whole story: a client can dump the full command namespace by sweeping single letters, and servers that hide the plain '/' reply still leak commands through per-letter prefixes. The FAWE crash works because the completion handler parses the input command recursively; a 4-deep loop body of nested for() statements overflows that parser. Anti-cheats ignore C14; anti-exploit plugins rate-limit completions, which is exactly what Plugins' Bypass mode cycles around.

implementation.overview: The tab-complete request packet and the protocol's least-guarded information oracle. Plugin enumeration (Rise 5.99 Plugins, Sigma PluginFinder), a FAWE command-parser crash (Rise 5.99 Crasher) and custom chat completion (Rise 6.x Chat) are the corpus families.
implementation.server_handling: processTabComplete: getTabCompletions(message, targetBlock) then S3APacketTabComplete with the results. No permission pre-check beyond what the dispatcher applies to the requesting player, no rate limit, no length cap beyond the String wire limit. Completions are computed against the live command registry, so plugin commands appear without any /plugins permission.
implementation.protocol_notes: VarInt-length-prefixed String + bool hasTargetBlock + optional BlockPos. The message does not need to start with '/' for the server to run the completion path. Replies are a String array; plugin-registered commands commonly appear as pluginname:command, which is the parsing key for enumeration tools.
implementation.anticheat_landscape: No anti-cheat measures C14. Anti-exploit and anti-spam plugins throttle completion requests per second; the '/a'..'/z' sweep is designed to stay under naive thresholds while still covering the namespace. The FAWE payload is a plugin-specific parser kill and is invisible to movement anti-cheats.

modules.name: Plugins
modules.purpose: Enumerate the server's plugin list through the tab-complete namespace and print it in chat.
modules.how_it_works: Normal mode sends C14('/') once and parses the S3A reply for completions. Bypass mode sends C14('/' + letter) for every letter of the alphabet to recover commands that servers filter from the plain dump; results are cached and the module disables after the sweep.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The per-letter sweep is the anti-throttle trade-off: slow enough to dodge naive rate limits, complete enough to enumerate hidden commands.
modules.variations: Sigma 4.11 implements the same idea as a one-shot command rather than a module.

modules.name: PluginFinder
modules.purpose: Discover plugins with a single '/'-completion and a 20 second listener window.
modules.how_it_works: The command sends C14('/'), registers an EventPacket listener, parses S3A completions for ':' prefixed names, prints the deduplicated plugin list and unregisters. A 20 second timer aborts the wait.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: One packet per invocation makes it effectively undetectable by rate-based guards; it trades completeness for stealth compared to Rise's alphabet sweep.
modules.variations: Rise 5.99 Plugins covers the same ground as a module with a Bypass mode; no other client has a C14 plugin finder.

modules.name: Crasher (FAWE)
modules.purpose: Crash FastAsyncWorldEdit by completing a pathologically nested command string.
modules.how_it_works: FAWE mode sends C14 with the nested '/to for(i=0;i<256;i++){...}' string every tick via sendPacketWithoutEvent.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Targets a plugin parser, not the anti-cheat; a patched FAWE just returns an error message. The one-packet-per-tick rate is unremarkable.
modules.variations: No equivalent tab-complete crash in the other 7 clients.

modules.name: Chat (custom tab complete)
modules.purpose: Drive the custom chat GUI's tab completion through C14 with a block position.
modules.how_it_works: The Chat module intercepts the tab key and sends C14PacketTabComplete(text, blockpos) via the vanilla send queue, then renders the S3A response in its own completion UI.
modules.vanilla_hook: Custom chat GUI key handler; no packet event hook on the send side.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: None; it mirrors vanilla completion behavior.
modules.variations: Same module file exists in Rise 6.1.30 with the identical send call.

implementation.general_hooks: S3APacketTabComplete is the receive-side hook for enumeration; the send side is direct construction (Rise 5.99, Sigma) or the vanilla send queue (Rise 6.x Chat).
implementation.client_variations: Rise 5.99 and Sigma construct the packet directly; Rise 6.x Chat goes through mc.thePlayer.sendQueue.addToSendQueue. Tenacity's PacketUtil whitelist also classifies C14 as a client packet.
